text: Lesson 48 named the bottleneck precisely: IX_Orders_CustomerID doesn't cover usp_CustomerOrderHistory, so every row triggers a Key Lookup, and the cost scales with a customer's order count. Chapter three covered exactly this class of fix. This lesson applies it -- one deliberate, targeted change, informed by what Lesson 48 actually measured.

usp_CustomerOrderHistory filters on CustomerID, orders by OrderDate descending, and selects OrderStatus, OrderTotal, and ShipDate. Chapter three's recipe: equality and filter columns go in the key, columns needed only for output go in INCLUDE, and where the query's ORDER BY matches, the sort column can go in the key too. CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Orders_CustomerID_OrderDate on dbo dot Orders, with CustomerID and OrderDate descending as the key, including OrderStatus, OrderTotal, and ShipDate. CustomerID stays the seek predicate. OrderDate descending in the key means the index is already sorted the way the query needs it -- no separate Sort operator, and the trailing-twelve-months filter narrows the seek range directly.

OrderStatus, OrderTotal, and ShipDate ride along in INCLUDE, so every column the SELECT needs is available right at the leaf level. There is no longer any reason for a Key Lookup -- the index itself now covers the query completely. That's the whole fix: one index, designed around exactly what Lesson 48's plan showed was missing.

Adding a covering index without removing the narrow one it replaces just means paying maintenance cost on two overlapping indexes instead of one. IX_Orders_CustomerID -- key: CustomerID only -- is now redundant; anything it could seek on, the new index seeks on too, plus it covers the query outright. DROP INDEX IX_Orders_CustomerID on dbo dot Orders. Dropping it isn't optional cleanup -- Meridian ships thousands of orders a day, and every INSERT into dbo dot Orders maintains every nonclustered index on the table. Leaving a superseded index in place is a permanent tax on every write, for zero remaining benefit.

Notice what this lesson doesn't do: it doesn't touch MAXDOP, doesn't rebuild unrelated indexes, doesn't add a NOLOCK hint to make the symptom go away without addressing the cause. Lesson 48 measured a specific operator at a specific scale. This lesson makes the one change that diagnosis calls for -- which is exactly what Lesson 50 will verify against.
